failure_summary.description: Calls mishandled endpoint-specific values or fields, including canonical forms, parameter buckets, and decomposing compound inputs.
Some calls used an endpoint that did not match the requested source or precise check.
A requested result was split across partial calls, or an optional value was added without being requested.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers endpoint matching, canonical values, and required/optional buckets, so those rules should not be duplicated. These edits clarify remaining actionable gaps: avoid speculative optional values, map compound inputs by field semantics, and combine qualifiers for one result into one call.

edits.content: - Populate optional fields only when the user requests the corresponding constraint or the field is necessary to express the requested result. Do not invent values for qualitative requests or translate them into arbitrary limits.

- When an endpoint represents a compound input with multiple semantic fields, split the input according to the documented field meanings and preserve all relevant components, including subdomains. Do not pass the whole compound value into one component or reduce a subdomain to its parent.

- When one endpoint handles a single requested result with multiple qualifiers, include all applicable parameters in one invocation. Do not make duplicate or partial calls merely to supply different qualifiers.
